title: A failed supernova?
caption: The irregular galaxy UGC 12682, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: UGC 12682 · constellation Pegasus · about 70 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Glowing warmly against a dark background, the irregular galaxy UGC 12682 looks distorted and oddly structured in this Hubble image, dotted with bright pockets where stars are forming. It lies approximately 70 million light-years away in Pegasus, the Winged Horse.

In November 2008, a 14-year-old from New York, Caroline Moore, discovered a supernova in this galaxy, becoming at the time the youngest person ever to find one. Professional follow-up observations showed that the explosion, named SN 2008ha, was odd in several ways. Its host galaxy rarely produces supernovae. It was one of the faintest supernovae ever seen, and it expanded very slowly afterwards, suggesting the blast released far less energy than expected.

Astronomers now classify SN 2008ha as a subclass of Type Ia supernova, the explosion of a white dwarf that has been pulling matter from a companion star. It may have been a partly failed supernova, which could explain why it did not destroy the whole star.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (1.69 x 1.55 arcminutes) and distance (70 million light years), the frame spans roughly 34,000 × 32,000 light-years. Its light set out about 70 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 imaged the galaxy through an ultraviolet and a visible filter. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Ultraviolet light is invisible to the eye, so part of this picture records light we could never see directly.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: A white dwarf is the dense leftover core of a star like the Sun. The image was taken with Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3.
alt: A distorted, irregular galaxy with bright patches of star formation against a dark background.
